rows.speaker: عن جده
rows.claim: An Anṣārī man asked whether God was near enough for whispered prayer or far away and requiring a call; the Prophet was silent, then the verse was revealed, promising a response when they pray.
rows.anchor: عن رجل من الأنصار عن أبيه عن جده قال جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet’s Companions asked where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال سأل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أين ربنا فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that a Bedouin asked where God was; the Prophet answered that He was in heaven upon His Throne, recited 20:5, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال سأل أعرابي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أين ربنا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Anas’s report, the Prophet answers the question about God’s whereabouts by saying He is in heaven upon the Throne, citing the Throne verse.
rows.anchor: قال: في السماء على عرشه ثم تلا (الرحمن على العرش استوى)

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that after the Prophet urged people not to tire of prayer and cited 40:60, a man asked whether God hears supplication; this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تعجزوا عن الدعاء

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: When 40:60 was revealed, people reportedly asked when to pray; this verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح أنه بلغه لما أنزلت

rows.speaker: سفيان عن أبي
rows.claim: Sufyan transmits from his father that Muslims asked whether God was near for whispered prayer or far away, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: من طريق سفيان عن أبي قال قال المسلمون يا رسول الله أقريب ربنا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد
rows.claim: When 40:60 was revealed, people asked how they could reach God to call upon Him; this verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد
rows.claim: After the verse’s revelation, the people reportedly affirmed that their Lord was truthful and everywhere.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: صدق ربنا وهو بكل مكان

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses responding to God as obeying Him, and explains that istijāba here means obedience.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: قال المسلمون: أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses believing in God here as knowing Him.
rows.anchor: وليؤمنوا بي} ليعلموا {فإني قريب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan gives an aphorism: ships are the keys to the seas, roads to the earth, and supplication to heaven.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: مفتاح البحار السفن ومفتاح الأرض

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb reports that Moses asked whether God was near or far; God said He accompanies whoever remembers Him and told Moses to remember Him in every state, including ritual impurity and relieving himself.
rows.anchor: عن كعب قال: قال موسى: أي رب أقريب أنت

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: During an expedition, the Prophet told companions to lower their voices: they called upon One who hears and sees, is neither deaf nor absent, and is nearer than a mount’s neck.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة فجعلنا لا نصعد شرفا

rows.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports God’s words: He is as His servant expects and is with the servant when called upon.
rows.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يقول الله: أنا عند ظن عبدي بي

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Salman reports that God is Living and Generous and is shy to return a servant’s raised hands empty; al-Tirmidhi graded the report good and al-Hakim called it sound.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن ربكم حي كريم يستحي من عبده إذا رفع يديه إليه أن يردهما صفرا

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muʿadh reports the Prophet saying that with true knowledge of God, mountains would move in response to one’s supplication.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لو عرفتم الله حق معرفته

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr says that supplication alongside righteousness is as sufficient as salt in food.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: يكفي من الدعاء مع البر ما يكفي الطعام من الملح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شبيب
rows.claim: When ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib prayed aloud beside Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Saʿid rebuked him for acting as if God were not near.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شبيب قال: صليت إلى جنب سعيد بن المسيب المغرب

rows.speaker: ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that whoever is granted an opening in supplication is granted the doors of response; al-Tirmidhi’s wording adds that the doors of mercy open and asking for well-being is especially beloved.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من فتح له في الدعاء

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: A saying transmitted by Ibrahim al-Taymi holds that one who praises God before supplicating has secured a response, while one who supplicates first remains hopeful.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي قال: كان يقال: إذا بدأ الرجل بالثناء

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman reports God saying at Adam’s creation that the servant asks and supplicates, while God answers.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان قال: لما خلق الله آدم قال: واحدة لي وواحدة لك

rows.speaker: نافع بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: Nafiʿ ibn Maʿd Yakrib reports that ʿAʾisha asked the Prophet about the verse; Gabriel conveyed God’s greeting and promise to answer her sincere, pious prayer.
rows.anchor: عن نافع بن معد يكرب قال: كنت أنا وعائشة فقالت سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas transmits Jābir’s report that the Prophet recited the verse and then prayed with the talbiya, affirmations of God’s oneness, the afterlife, Paradise, Hell, the Hour, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ

words: وقاتلوا في سبيل الله الذين يقاتلونكم ولا تعتدوا
rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz explains the prohibition on transgression as barring fighting women and children who have not taken up arms against the Muslims.
rows.anchor: كتبت إلي عمر بن عبد العزيز أسأله عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the command to kill wherever they are found refers to the polytheists.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {واقتلوهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses thaqiftumūhum as finding them and cites Hassan’s line about Banu Luʾayy as Arab usage.
rows.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {ثقفتموهم} قال: وجدتموهم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya glosses fitna as associating partners with God, which he says is worse than killing.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya also explains that the fitna the audience persists in is greater than killing.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says a believer’s return to idol worship is worse for him than being killed while in the right.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {والفتنة أشد من القتل}

rows.speaker: عاصم من طريق أبي بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash transmits that ʿAsim reads the forms with alif, except the final faqtulūhum, which is without alif.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم {ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقاتلوكم فيه فإن قاتلوكم} كلها بالألف

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says he heard Abu Ishaq read all the forms without alif.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص قال: شمعت أبا اسحق يقرؤهن كلهن بغير ألف

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash says the followers of ʿAbd Allah read all the forms without alif.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش قال: كان أصحاب عبد الله يقرؤونها كلهن بغير ألف

words: ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقاتلوكم فيه
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the rule was to wait until they initiated fighting in the Sacred Mosque, but it was later abrogated by 2:193’s command to fight until fitna ceased.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقاتلوكم فيه}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Sacred Mosque and sacred-month restrictions remained in force until both were abrogated by 9:5.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses their desisting as repentance.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فإن انتهوا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses fitna as associating partners with God and says the religion is to be made purely monotheistic for God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة} يقول: شرك بالله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads the command as allowing fighting only against those who fight the Muslims.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد {وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة} قال: لا تقاتلوا إلا من قاتلكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says 2:193 superseded the earlier sanctuary restriction: fitna means shirk, and religion belonging to God means fighting until the testimony of God’s oneness is proclaimed, for that purpose the Prophet fought and called people.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ولا تقاتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقاتلوكم فيه فكان هذا كذا حتى نسخ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Qatada transmits the saying that God commanded the Prophet to fight people until they profess that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: وذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول إن الله أمرني

words: فإن انتهوا فلا عدوان إلا على الظالمين
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the wrongdoer who refuses to say there is no god but God is fought until he says it.
rows.anchor: قال: وإن الظالم الذي أبى أن يقول: لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ glosses religion belonging to God as worship being directed to God alone.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع {ويكون الدين لله} يقول: حتى لا يعبد إلا الله

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the wrongdoers as those who refuse to profess that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة {فلا عدوان إلا على الظالمين} قال: هم من أبى أن يقول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: During Ibn al-Zubayr’s civil conflict, Ibn ʿUmar rejected using this verse to justify revolt: he said fighting had ended when fitna ceased and religion was God’s, while his questioners sought renewed fitna and religion for other than God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه أتاه رجلان في فتنة ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed after hypocrites mocked the Muslims killed in the expedition that included ʿAsim and Mirthad, saying the men had neither stayed with their families nor delivered the Prophet’s message.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما أصيبت السرية

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that the man’s speech outwardly displays Islam, while his heart contradicts what his tongue says.
rows.anchor: أي لما يظهر من الإسلام بلسانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the description as someone who argues fiercely and answers back whenever addressed.
rows.anchor: {وهو ألد الخصام} أي ذو جدال إذا كلمك راجعك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbas’s account, when the man leaves, he acts to corrupt the land and destroy crops and offspring; God neither loves nor approves his work.
rows.anchor: خرج من عندك (سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies those who sell themselves for God’s pleasure as the members of that expedition, who gave themselves in jihad and fulfilled God’s due until they died.
rows.anchor: الذين شروا أنفسهم من الله بالجهاد في سبيله والقيام بحقه حتى هلكوا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq names the Quraysh men who joined in killing Khubayb: ʿIkrima ibn Abi Jahl, Saʿid ibn ʿAbd Allah, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, ʿUbayda ibn Hakim, and Umayya ibn Abi ʿUtba.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحق قال: كان الذين أجلبوا على خبيب في قتله نفر من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuing report says the verse concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who professed sincere Islam to the Prophet in Medina, impressed him, then burned a Muslim’s crops and hamstrung his donkeys after leaving.
rows.anchor: قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي حليف لبني زهرة أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse refers to al-Akhnas ibn Shariq; a descendant of al-Akhnas asked him not to name anyone until leaving Mecca, claiming the Qur’an was revealed about Meccans.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي قال: كنت جالسا بمكة فسألوني عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Saʿid al-Maqburi quotes a divine warning about honeyed tongues, bitter hearts, and using religion for worldly gain; Muhammad ibn Kaʿb identifies its subject with this verse, and Saʿid says he knew its particular referent.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد المقبري أنه ذاكر محمد بن كعب القرظي

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the verse may have been revealed about one man while remaining general in application afterward.
rows.anchor: فقال محمد بن كعب: إن الآية تنزل في الرجل تكون عامة بعد

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas transmits a divine warning to a prophet about people with soft sheep skins, honeyed speech, bitter hearts, and false reliance on God; God threatens a bewildering trial and calls believers to trust Him.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: أوحى الله إلى نبي من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb reports God rebuking Israelite scholars who pursue worldly gain through religious learning, burden others with religion, and exploit orphans and widows; God swears to send a trial that confounds the wise.
rows.anchor:
عن وهب
إن الرب تبارك وتعالى قال لعلماء بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses aladd al-khiṣām as severe in disputation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وهو ألد الخصام} قال: شديد الخصومة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In response to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn ʿAbbas explains the phrase as a disputant who argues falsely and cites a line by Muhalhil as Arabic evidence.
rows.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله قوله {وهو ألد الخصام} قال: الجدل المخاصم في الباطل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid describes the contentious person as unjust and not upright.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد {وهو ألد الخصام} قال: ظالم لا يستقيم

rows.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: ʿAʾisha reports the Prophet saying that the most hateful men to God are the contentious adversaries.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet lists four traits of a complete hypocrite: betraying trust, lying, breaking a pact, and speaking abusively in an argument; any one is a trait of hypocrisy until abandoned.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet saying that continual disputation is sufficient to make a person sinful.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كفى بك آثما

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Dardaʾ says continual disputation suffices for sin, continual hostility for injustice, and continual talk about God for lying.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: كفى بك آثما أن لا تزال مماريا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Dardaʾ says much speech brings much lying, frequent oaths bring much sin, and frequent quarrels endanger one’s religion.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: من كثر كلامه كثر كذبه

rows.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari says that no scrupulously pious person has ever quarreled.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الكريم الجزري قال: ما خاصم ورع قط

rows.speaker: ابن شبرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Shubrumah says excessive quarrelling is sinful; he also transmits maxims linking poor restraint in dispute with inability to bear truth and praising patience and chastity.
rows.anchor: عن ابن شبرمة قال: من بالغ في الخصومة أثم ومن قصر فيها خصم ولا يطيق الحق

rows.speaker: الأحنف بن قيس
rows.claim: Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays says three types cannot prevail fairly over three others, including a forbearing person over a fool and a virtuous person over a profligate.
rows.anchor: عن الأحنف بن قيس قال: ثلاثة لا ينتصفون من ثلاثة حليم من أحمق وبر من فاجر

rows.speaker: ابن عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla says when two men trade insults, the more ignoble one always wins.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمرو بن العلاء قال: ما تشاتم رجلان قط إلا غلب ألأمهما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the man’s striving as working in the land, the tilth as its plants, and offspring as the young of all animals, humans and beasts.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض} قال: عمل في الأرض {ويهلك الحرث}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says unjust rule and oppression lead God to withhold rain, destroying crops and offspring; he links this to 30:41, where corruption on land and sea comes from human deeds.
rows.anchor:
عن مجاهد
أنه سئل عن قوله {وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض} قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the tilth as crops and offspring as the young of every animal.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن قوله {ويهلك الحرث والنسل} قال: الحرث الزرع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas adds that the offspring of every animal includes people as well.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: النسل نسل كل دابة الناس أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses offspring as birds and beasts and cites a line of poetry using nasl for descendants as Arabic evidence.
rows.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله {الحرث والنسل}

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says a pilgrim lacking sandals may wear leather socks and, when asked whether to slit them, invokes God’s dislike of corruption as reason not to cut them.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: يتخفف المحرم إذا لم يجد نعلين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says it is a grave sin for a man told by his brother to fear God to respond by telling him to mind his own business.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن من أكبر الذنب عند الله أن يقول الرجل

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan reports that when a man told Malik ibn Mughawil to fear God, Malik placed his cheek on the ground in humility before God.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان قال: قال رجل لمالك بن مغول: اتق الله فقط

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A man admonished ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab to fear God; ʿUmar said there is no good in us if others do not admonish us, nor in them if they do not speak up.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن أن رجلا قال لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: اتق الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the wretched resting place as what its inhabitants prepared for themselves.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولبئس المهاد} قال: بئس ما مهدوا لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: صهيب
rows.claim: Suhayb reports that Quraysh let him emigrate to the Prophet after he surrendered his property; the Prophet welcomed him saying his sale had profited twice.
rows.anchor: عن صهيب قال لما أردت الهجرة من مكة إلى النبي

words: ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغاء مرضات الله
rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says Quraysh pursued Suhayb as he emigrated; he offered his property and holdings for release, and the verse was revealed when the Prophet welcomed him as a profitable seller.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال أقبل صهيب مهاجرا نحو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتبعه نفر من قريش

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed about both Suhayb ibn Sinan and Abu Dharr.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {ومن الناس من يشري نفسه} قال: نزلت في صهيب بن سنان وأبي ذر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the verse concerns Suhayb, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Jundab ibn al-Sakan; Abu Dharr escaped his pursuers twice, while Suhayb bought his freedom by surrendering his remaining property.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {ومن الناس من يشري نفسه} الآية قال نزلت في صهيب بن سنان وأبي ذر الغفاري

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An incomplete report counsels placing the matter in what is lawful and avoiding the forbidden: God alone creates, guides, and provides, and controls life and death while the person earns reward.
rows.anchor: قال: فأنت خلقته قلت: بل الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that intercourse with one’s wife each Friday earns two rewards, the man’s ritual bath and his wife’s bath.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيعجز أحدكم أن يجامع أهله في كل يوم جمعة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar says he makes himself have intercourse in hope that God will bring forth from him a soul that glorifies Him.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال والله إني لأكره نفسي على الجماع رجاء أن يخرج الله مني نسمة تسبح

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that when a woman complained that her husband did not approach her, ʿUmar asked about their frequency and told her that intercourse once each period of purity was sufficient.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال بلغني أنه جاءت امرأة إلى عمر بن الخطاب فقالت إن زوجها لا يصيبها

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الأنصارية
rows.claim: Asma bint Yazid says she was the first divorcee for whom a waiting period was established by revelation, after she was divorced in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن الانصارية قالت: طلقت على عهد رسول الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that in pre-Islamic practice a man could divorce without imposing any waiting period.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} قال: كان أهل الجاهلية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the waiting-period rule was specified by 65:4 for women past menstruation and those who do not menstruate, and excludes women divorced before consummation under 33:49.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس {والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء} {واللائي يئسن من المحيض
